crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Finding Acquisition Targets
children.blurb: Finding acquisition targets in private equity and deal sourcing means using AI to identify, screen, and rank companies that fit a fund's investment thesis.

children.name: Data Room Diligence
children.blurb: Data room diligence in private equity and deal sourcing covers the structured review of a target company's documents during due diligence, including financial statements, contracts, customer lists, intellectual property, employment records, litigation and regulatory filings.

children.name: Buyout Modelling
children.blurb: Buyout modelling covers the construction and stress-testing of leveraged buyout financial models, including sources and uses, debt schedules, operating forecasts, and sponsor returns.

children.name: Private Market Valuation
children.blurb: Private market valuation covers the pricing of equity and debt in companies that are not publicly traded, with a focus on AI businesses where traditional financials may be thin and intangible assets dominate.

children.name: Tracking Synergies After a Merger
children.blurb: Tracking synergies after a merger means monitoring whether the combined entity achieves the cost savings, revenue gains, and operational improvements that justified the deal.

sections.body: Private equity and deal sourcing uses AI to scan company databases, news, and filings for acquisition candidates, to read data room documents during due diligence, to build financial models for leveraged buyouts, to estimate prices for private companies, and to track whether merged businesses hit expected savings. In practice, tools now flag companies that match a fund's criteria, extract key clauses from contracts, and compare a target's metrics against similar deals. The site's 352 merger and acquisition filings and 432 company pages give these systems a factual base to work from. This is not a prediction engine, it is a search and summarization layer over messy corporate data.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Finding targets and reading data rooms are the most mature, because they rely on text search and document classification, which are well understood. Buyout modelling and private valuation are harder, because private companies lack public prices and comparable data is sparse. AI can produce a model quickly, but it cannot know if a supplier contract will be renewed or if a founder will stay. Tracking synergies after a merger is still mostly manual, since cost savings depend on operational decisions that happen after the deal closes. The honest limit is that AI narrows the list and speeds up reading, but the final price and the decision to buy remain human judgments.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader would start with Finding Acquisition Targets to see how AI screens thousands of companies for fit, then move to Data Room Diligence to understand how it reads contracts and flags risks during due diligence. Buyout Modelling shows how the same tools build debt and cash flow projections for a leveraged purchase, while Private Market Valuation explains why pricing a private company is different from pricing a public one. Finally, Tracking Synergies After a Merger covers what happens after the deal, where AI tries to measure whether promised cost cuts and revenue gains actually appear. Together these pages follow the deal from first search to post-close review.
